translations.source_sense_description: etwas sehr, sehr schlecht erledigen oder behandeln, so dass es missglückt oder zerstört ist

glosses: To make a mess of; to untidy, disorder, soil, or muss.

examples.text: The afternoon breeze messed up my hair.
[…] kwatumas, those aggressive and sharp-toothed eels that so thoroughly mess up one's tackle when hooked […]

glosses: To cause a problem with; to introduce an error or mistake in; to make muddled or confused; spoil; ruin.

examples.text: The change messed something up, and it's not working anymore.

glosses: To botch, bungle; to perform poorly on.

examples.text: Well, I messed up my solo, but otherwise it was a good concert.

glosses: To make a mistake; to do something incorrectly; to perform poorly.

examples.text: She messed up on her final exam.
He has a hard time getting started because he's afraid he'll mess up.

glosses: To cause (another person) to make unwanted mistakes in a given task, usually through distraction or obnoxious behavior.

examples.text: Stop bumping me! You keep messing me up!
He messed up his elbow at the track meet.

glosses: To manhandle; beat up; rough up.

examples.text: Her brother's friends messed him up a little after he cheated on her.

glosses: To discombobulate, utterly confuse, or confound psychologically; to throw into a state of mental disarray.

examples.text: That girl totally messed me up, man. I'm not sure who I am anymore.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas sehr, sehr schlecht erledigen oder behandeln, so dass es missglückt oder zerstört ist

glosses: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.

examples.text: The Veian and the Gabian towirs shall fall, / And one promiscuous ruin cover all; / Nor, after length of years, a stone betray / The place where once the very ruins lay.
The labour of a day will not build up a virtuous habit on the ruins of an old and vicious character.

A canister of flour from the kitchen had been thrown at the looking-glass and lay like trampled snow over the remains of a decent blue suit with the lining ripped out which lay on top of the ruin of a plastic wardrobe.
Dr. Manuel: No one is saved. The age of humanity is ended. Soon, only ruin and corpses will remain.
Not only is Jerusalem not a ruin, but she is at the height of her glory compared to all of Jewish history!

glosses: The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.

examples.text: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

glosses: Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.

examples.text: Gambling has been the ruin of many.
The errors of young men are the ruin of business.

The Bat—they called him the Bat.[…]. He[…]played a lone hand,[…]. Most lone wolves had a moll at any rate—women were their ruin—but if the Bat had a moll, not even the grapevine telegraph could locate her.
His ruin startled th’ other steeds.

glosses: A change that destroys or defeats something; destruction; overthrow.

examples.text: the ruin of a ship or an army
the ruin of a constitution or a government
the ruin of health or hopes

Oh Portius, is there not some choſen Curſe,
Some hidden Thunder in the Stores of Heav’n,
Red with uncommon Wrath, to blaſt the Man
Who owes his Greatneſs to his Country’s Ruin?
Ruin seize thee, ruthless king!

glosses: To cause the fiscal ruin of; to bankrupt or drive out of business.

examples.text: With all these purchases, you surely mean to ruin us!
In one way, indeed, he bade fair to ruin us; for he kept on staying week after week, and at last month after month, so that all the money had been long exhausted...

glosses: To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.

examples.text: He ruined his new white slacks by accidentally spilling oil on them.
By the fireside there are old men seated, / Seeing ruined cities in the ashes.

glosses: To upset or overturn the plans or progress of, or to have a disastrous effect on something.

examples.text: My car breaking down just as I was on the road ruined my vacation.

glosses: To make something less enjoyable or likeable.

examples.text: I used to love that song, but being assaulted when that song was playing ruined the song for me.

glosses: To reveal the ending of (a story); to spoil.
To fall into a state of decay.

examples.text: Though he his house of polisht marble build, / Yet shall it ruine like the Moth's fraile cell

glosses: To seduce or debauch, and thus harm the social standing of.

examples.text: The young libertine was notorious for ruining local girls.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas sehr, sehr schlecht erledigen oder behandeln, so dass es missglückt oder zerstört ist

glosses: Construire en torchis, c'est à dire en utilisant entre autre de la boue.

examples.text: Faute de pierre, on bousille dans ce pays.
C’est un brouillon, il ne fait que bousiller.
— Oui, tes yeux vont se brouiller, tu vas bousiller et tu auras encore « du refusé ».
J’ai remarqué que, à de rares exceptions près, les hommes bousillent leur travail.
Il a bousillé l’ouvrage.

J’ai des envies nouvelles, avoir le bac et larguer les bonnes sœurs pour faire philo au lycée, cette année-là, cette classe-là que j’attends comme une révélation, il ne faut pas que la religion me la bousille.
Mardi était notre jour sacré, je n'allais pas tout bousiller pour une chouinerie de gamin. Tiens, pour un peu plus encore, j'en aurais chialé.

… un tonnerre d’applaudissements roule dans le cabaret, mais je vous prie de croire qu’il stoppe net quand la salle entière s’aperçoit qu’on a bel et bien bousillé Willie le Pigeon. Il était affalé en avant et sa tête avait renversé le pot de fleurs placé au centre de la table.

C’est ce qu’il fera bientôt, probablement au petit matin, avant que tout le monde rentre à la maison pour les fêtes. Comme on souhaite éviter que le président vienne tout bousiller avec son veto, il faudra se contenter du plus petit dénominateur commun, qui risque de ne satisfaire personne.
« Des mecs comme ça, il faudrait les bousiller tout de suite », répondit mon tortionnaire.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas sehr, sehr schlecht erledigen oder behandeln, so dass es missglückt oder zerstört ist

glosses: ухудшить что-либо, сделать плохим, негодным, некрасивым

examples.text: Говорили, что так мяч можно испортить, но нам было всё равно.
Илья Фомич называет её взбалмошной девчонкой, которую мать испортила баловством.
Господин ты мой, клянусь богом // И пречистым именем Марии, // Пред тобою я не виновата, // Испортили меня злые люди.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas sehr, sehr schlecht erledigen oder behandeln, so dass es missglückt oder zerstört ist
etwas sehr, sehr schlecht erledigen oder behandeln, so dass es missglückt oder zerstört ist

jemandem etwas kaputt machen oder den Spaß an etwas verderben

examples.text: The terrorists have really mucked up our holiday plans.
That’s why they’re called the Founders? Yes, because it will be their job to repair a world that millennials have mucked up beyond repair.

“Looking at our season so far, we have to be honest and admit that we mucked it up ourselves,” Özil told the German website spox.com. “We did not play to our potential in the games against the so-called smaller teams. You immediately get punished for that in the Premier League.

He said that this was simply a “historical fact” and that he could “see no reason why every other country in the world should be prevented from feeling pride in itself because the Germans mucked up twice in a century”.

glosses: To clown around; to have fun, often at the expense of others.

examples.text: It's the last day of school and everyone is mucking up.
